small_guidance:
- Increase BLOCK_SP to 1024 or 2048 and drop BLOCK_OC to 32 to reduce per-tile redundant input loads; sweep (BLOCK_OC=32/64, BLOCK_SP=512/1024/2048) with num_warps=4/8 via `triton.autotune`.
- The inner loop reloads each x value IC*KH*KW=72 times per output tile via overlapping windows — try a layout where each program loads a padded input strip once into SRAM (load (IC, BLOCK_SP_H+2, BLOCK_SP_W+2) once) and then does the 3×3 convolution from SRAM, removing the redundant gathers.
- Reduce num_stages to 2 (the current 3 wastes shared memory on a compute-bound inner loop) and consider splitting the spatial reduction across a third grid dim with atomic adds to expose more parallelism (currently only 128 programs given OC=64,BLOCK_OC=64).
large_guidance:
- Restructure as an im2col-style GEMM: one program per (N, OC tile, output-spatial tile) with K=IC*KH*KW=72 as the GEMM-K reduction using `tl.dot`, instead of the current outer-product accumulation. This unlocks tensor-core-style matmul throughput which the current scalar FMA loop misses.
- Grid is currently only N*ceil(OC/BLOCK_OC)=128 programs on a 128-SM-class GPU — way under-occupied. Split the output spatial axis into the grid (3D grid: N, OC tile, SP tile) and do a final pool reduction either via a second small kernel or via atomic-add into a per-(N,OC) accumulator. This is the highest-leverage change.
- Use channels-last input layout (NHWC) so the IC dimension is the innermost contiguous axis, making the K-loop in the GEMM coalesce naturally; permute weight to (OC, KH, KW, IC) to match.
